## AI use

<!--
  Required on every PR. Name what you used and what you used it for — e.g.
  "Claude, to work out why my training loop wasn't converging."
  If you didn't use any, write "None." That's a real answer, not a wrong one.

  Acknowledged use is ordinary professional practice. Unacknowledged use is an
  academic integrity violation under the syllabus. Note also that AI-generated
  code is not permitted for the from-scratch implementations themselves — help
  understanding a bug you wrote is fine; having it write the implementation is not.
-->

## Before you request a review

- [ ] The **title names the change** — `[WeekN] <Title>`, not "stuff" or "updates"
- [ ] The description above says **what** and **why**
- [ ] **AI use declared** above — "None" counts
- [ ] **Small and focused** — only the files that belong to this change
- [ ] **Useful comments** in the code — yes, even for print statements
- [ ] No leftover debug prints (`print("asdf")`, stray `# testing` blocks)
